subject: Latency trigger gate activation authority — model-sigma (Sigmatech)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-08 08:13:22 -0700
Subject: [ALERT] model-sigma p95 > SLA threshold for Sigmatech — authorization required

Karthik,

Monitoring surfaced a sustained p95 latency spike for model-sigma serving Sigmatech (customer-critical route) starting 08:05 PDT. Current metrics: p95 = 1.86s (SLA = 1.2s), error-rate unchanged. Rolling 5m window shows degradation across two availability zones.

Automated rollback gate is "primed" (telemetry-based), but per the customer contract we need explicit account-level authorization to activate the automated circuit-breaker and divert traffic to the fallback variant (model-sigma-lite). The default mitigation path would:
- enable fallback variant for 30% of traffic (gradual ramp over 5 min)
- turn on prefix KV caching for affected keys
- enable dark-traffic sampling to evaluate regenerated outputs
- create a rollback ticket and notify infra for resource scaling

I attached the telemetry CSV with per-AZ p95 and a short playbook excerpt. Please advise if you authorize activation OR if you prefer a manual canary instead. We should decide within the next 30 minutes to avoid further SLA exposure.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. SRE — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sigmatech_p95_telemetry_09082028.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Theo Baxter <theo@sigmatech.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-08 08:28:10 -07:00
Subject: Latency trigger gate activation authority — model-sigma (Sigmatech)

Theo —

Quick note from our ops team: we observed a p95 latency regression on model-sigma affecting your account. We want to avoid ongoing customer impact and are proposing a controlled diversion to a fallback variant while we investigate. Summary of the proposed action (non-destructive, reversible):

Plan:
- Activate the automated mitigation gate for Sigmatech, diverting 30% of production traffic to model-sigma-lite over a 5-minute ramp.
- Keep a full dark-traffic mirror of production requests to model-sigma (no external users see those outputs).
- Retain full request/response telemetry and KV cache snapshots for later root-cause analysis.
- If no regression is observed in 30 minutes, we will progressively increase the fallback share; if errors increase we will revert immediately.

SLA impact: estimated effective p95 for visible traffic should return under SLA for the customer route within 10–20 minutes; we will notify you of any service credit exposure.

We've attached the operational playbook and the telemetry snapshot. To proceed with the automated gate we need either written authorization from you (reply to this thread) or approval from Redwood exec (Ben). If you prefer a manual canary I can coordinate but that will delay mitigation by ~30–45 minutes while infra stages the canary cluster.

Let me know which you prefer — immediate activation (customer auth) OR manual canary. If I don't hear back in 20 minutes I'll escalate for exec approval to avoid extended SLA violation.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Reliability (Americas)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollout_playbook_model_sigma_v2.pdf

From: Theo Baxter <theo@sigmatech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sigmatech Procurement <procurement@sigmatech.com>
Date: 2028-09-08 09:02:47 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency trigger gate activation authority — model-sigma (Sigmatech)

Karthik —

Thanks for the heads up. We are sensitive to any change that could alter inference outputs for a live feature. A few clarifications before we green-light automated diversion: 

1) Will any user-facing responses be generated from the fallback model that differ materially? We need guarantees that the observable behavior for end users on our critical routes will not be semantically broken.
2) Please provide the audit log slice for the past hour (request IDs) and the dark-traffic replay sample so our ML ops team can sanity-check.
3) If there is measurable SLA remediation lag > 15 minutes we will expect a proportional credit as described in section 4.2 of our contract. Please confirm the credit calculation you will apply if the p95 remains out of SLA for more than 1 hour.

Procurement: if we confirm authorization, can you provide a one-click DocuSign or a simple signed confirmation to satisfy our internal change control?

If you can get all of the above into this thread quickly I will try to get procurement to sign off.

—Theo
Product Lead, Sigmatech

On Sep 8, 2028, at 08:28, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Theo —
> 
> Quick note from our ops team: we observed a p95 latency regression on model-sigma affecting your account...

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-08 12:45:05 -07:00
Subject: RE: Latency trigger gate activation authority — model-sigma (Sigmatech)

Karthik / Neha —

Approve activation of the automated gate and the 30% diversion to model-sigma-lite for Sigmatech. This aligns with our SLA playbook for high-tier accounts and is preferable to letting the p95 remain elevated. Please proceed with the following constraints: 
- Maintain dark-traffic mirroring and keep raw telemetry for a minimum of 30 days for audit.
- Surface the per-minute rollout dashboard link to Sigmatech (Ops should post to the drive link in-thread).
- If Sigmatech procurement signs the DocuSign, capture the signed artifact on the ticket and mark for billing credit evaluation if remediation >1h.

I attached a signed authorization stub for now to keep the customer moving. Follow-up: schedule a postmortem with the model team within 48 hours.

Ben Carter
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: authorization_form_signed_stub.pdf
